newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks mostly lower in shrinking trade.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks mostly lower in shrinking trade.

text.p: Croatian stocks were mostly weaker on Wednesday, as leading issues held their ground in shrinking trade.
Traders blamed the depression on the circumspection of foreign investors who stood back because of high stock prices and Western political pressures on Croatia.
"The downward trend is continuing and I cannot see it reversed before the autumn, before prices have fallen another 20 to 30 percent," a market analyst said.
"It seems that foreign investors have turned to other markets, including Romania and Poland, where share prices are lower," he said.
The most liquid Croatian stocks are too expensive given the return they offer, he said, adding that many 1996 results had been worse than expected.

Of the three fully-listed firms, only Zagrebacka Banka gained 45 kuna to close at 2,050 on meagre volume of 118 shares. Drugs firm Pliva stayed flat at 440 kuna, trading 927 shares, and so did Varazdinska Banka at 270 kuna, trading only 81 shares.

Confectioner Kras and food concern Podravka both lost five kuna to close at 400 and 255 kuna respectively. The two jointly accounted for more than two thirds of the day's trading, both selling in excess of 2,000 shares.

The tourist firms continued losing value. Leading Istrian hotelier Plava Laguna, which was trading at around 1,400 kuna with little oscillation for most of the year, slumped 180 kuna to 1,200. Laguna was the biggest decliner.

Another market participant, who also blamed the slow trade and sliding prices on the absence of foreign investors, said they were scared because of recent public criticism the country's leadership had received from the United States.

U.S. Secretary of State, Madeleine Albright, recently lambasted senior Croatian officials for not allowing Serb refugees to return to their homes and failing to turn war crime suspects over to the U.N. tribunal in The Hague.
"Some strong words were used, which left an impression of political uncertainty which always scares foreigners away," the trader said.
Seven of 11 active issues fell, two rose and three were flat. Volume was down at 6,958 units and so was turnover, at 2.8 million kuna.
The biggest gainer, electrical manufacturer Koncar, added 10 kuna to 980 on volume of 75.
